lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Cerberus — we're practically family, you and I, both being dogs — tell me, by the Styx: what was Socrates like when he came down to your place? You're a god, so presumably you can do more than bark — you can speak like a human when you feel like it.

lines.speaker: Cerberus
lines.text: From a distance, Menippus, he gave every appearance of approaching with an unflinching expression, looking as though he wasn't the least bit afraid of death — and very keen to make sure the people standing outside the entrance noticed. But once he'd leaned in over the chasm and got a look at the dark — and I gave his foot a nip, since the hemlock was taking its time — [pause] well. He wailed like an infant, sobbed over his own little children, went completely to pieces.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: So the man was a fraud, then? He didn't actually despise the business at all?

lines.speaker: Cerberus
lines.text: No — but once he saw it was unavoidable, he put on a bold face, as if he were going to suffer willingly what he was going to suffer regardless. For the audience. To be admired. [pause] And really, I could say the same about all of them. Up to the threshold: bold, manly, fearless. Once they're inside: the truth comes out.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: And me? How did I look coming down?

lines.speaker: Cerberus
lines.text: You, Menippus — alone, and worthy of the breed. You and Diogenes before you. Because you didn't have to be forced in, or shoved. You came of your own accord. [pause] Laughing. Telling everyone else to go weep.
